questions.question: A stratum is:
options: A single layer of sedimentary rock laid down as a sheet, one of many stacked strata

questions.question: Differential erosion happens in the Karoo because:
options: All the layers erode at the same speed
The layers are UNEQUAL in resistance — weak shale is stripped fast while tough dolerite and sandstone survive
Erosion only attacks the bottom layer
The rock contains no layers at all

questions.question: The dolerite sills of the Karoo formed when:
options: Magma injected itself between the flat strata about one hundred and eighty-three million years ago and cooled into hard horizontal sheets
Rivers deposited gravel in old channels

questions.question: The high plateau of Lesotho behaves like horizontal strata because it is built of:
options: Stacked horizontal basalt LAVA flows, each acting as a resistant cap

subtopics.title: From Plateau to Pointed Koppie — the Landform Family

questions.question: The steep rim that edges a plateau is called:
options: An ESCARPMENT — southern Africa's Great Escarpment is the grandest example

questions.question: The proportion test that separates a mesa from a butte says:
options: A mesa is always made of basalt and a butte of shale
A mesa is broader than it is tall; a butte is taller than it is broad, with only a small flat crown
A mesa has no flat top
A butte is always the larger of the two

questions.question: Teebus and Koffiebus near Steynsburg are famous because they are:
options: A pair of dolerite-capped flat-topped hills showing the mesa and butte stages side by side
Sand dunes on a coastal plain

questions.question: Spandau Kop outside Graaff-Reinet illustrates the stage that follows the breaching of the cap, namely:
options: The CONICAL HILL — soft strata exposed on all sides weather back into a smooth pointed koppie

questions.question: The defining feature of scarp retreat is that the cliff:
options: Is rebuilt at the SAME steep angle a little further back each time — the slope retreats parallel to itself
Gets flatter and rounder each century

questions.question: Down wasting differs from back wasting because down wasting:
options: Moves slopes sideways at constant angle
Lowers the landscape from the top, sinking summits and rounding every profile

questions.question: Capped horizontal strata favour back wasting because:
options: The soft rock is on top
The cap locks the summit at its height, so the landform can only yield inward from its edges
There is no frost in the Karoo

questions.question: A pediplain is best described as:
options: The steep face of an escarpment
A vast, almost level erosion surface formed where the pediments of scarps retreating from opposite sides meet and merge

subtopics.title: Canyons and the Mapwork of Flat Country

questions.question: The walls of a canyon in horizontal strata descend in giant steps because:
options: Each resistant band stands as a sheer face while each weak band wears back into a slope
The river carves steps on purpose
Wind erosion polishes the walls evenly

questions.question: On a contour map, the summit of a mesa appears as:
options: A spiral of contours winding to a peak
A strikingly EMPTY area inside closed contours, ringed by tightly bunched contours marking the cliff
Evenly spaced contours right across the top

questions.question: A cross-section uses a vertical scale of 1 cm to 25 m against a horizontal map scale of 1:50 000. The vertical exaggeration is:
options: 20 times — the vertical scale is 1:2 500, and 50 000 divided by 2 500 gives 20

questions.question: Land climbs 150 m over a horizontal distance of 3 000 m. The gradient is:
options: 1 in 20 — height over distance in the same units, 150 over 3 000 simplified

subtopics.title: The Paving Slab on the Sand Heap

questions.question: In the builder's-yard picture, the concrete paving slab stands for:
options: The hard dolerite cap that shields the soft layers beneath it

questions.question: The rain strips the yard but leaves a column standing under the slab because:
options: The column is made of harder sand
Soft material exposed to the weather goes first while protected material survives — differential erosion
Rain never falls on flat ground

questions.question: A dead-flat horizon in the Karoo tells you:
options: The land was levelled by the sea last century
There is no rock beneath the surface
An unbroken hard cap is still lying up there on guard

questions.question: In the shape code, box, tower and tent stand for:
A tower becomes a tent at the moment when:
options: The hill grows a new cap
The cap is finally punched through, and the unprotected soft rock rounds into a smooth cone

questions.question: The full countdown of the landform family reads:
options: Floor, box, tower, tent, flat — plateau, mesa, butte, conical hill, plain

questions.question: A single Karoo viewpoint is special to geographers because it often shows:
options: Several generations of the landform family — mesa, butte and cone — sharing one horizon

questions.question: Saying the wall walks away means that Karoo cliffs:
options: Stay just as steep while their position shifts steadily backwards — parallel retreat
Sag into round hills as they age
Erode only at their base and lean forward

questions.question: The winter half of the walking mechanism is:
options: Ice freezing and swelling in the cap's cracks, popping blocks off the cliff face

questions.question: The footprint a walking wall leaves at its foot is:
options: The PEDIMENT — a smooth, gently sloping rock floor that later merges with others into a pediplain

questions.question: When a mighty river attacks horizontal strata it cuts:
options: Straight DOWN, sawing out a canyon with stepped walls — the Blyde River Canyon is South Africa's showpiece
